incentives.name: Douglas County business personal property tax rebate (Flexential Parker)
incentives.what: Rebates 100% of the county's share of business personal property tax over 35 years for Flexential's Parker data center; approved August 2026.

incentives.name: No statewide data center tax exemption
incentives.what: Colorado has no data center sales tax exemption: the 2025 bill and HB26-1030 (2026) both failed (see laws_and_bills).

dockets.utility: Public Service Company of Colorado (Xcel Energy)
dockets.what: Advice Letter 2018-Electric: new large-load rate class for new or added loads of 50 MW or more, transmission cost changes, optional Clean Transition Tariff and Speed-to-Market Pathway; 15-year contracts, financial assurance and exit fees (Denver Post via search summary). PUC suspended the filing; interim decision C26-0396-I (June 15, 2026). SWEEP and Rewiring America sought intervention (May 21, 2026). An advocacy page says a hearing was set for Aug. 25, 2026 (not confirmed with the PUC).

laws_and_bills.name: HB26-1030 Data Center & Utility Modernization
laws_and_bills.what: Would have created a data center development authority and a 100% state sales and use tax exemption for 20 years (plus possible 10-year extension) for certified centers investing at least $250M; postponed indefinitely 11-2 by House Energy & Environment Committee on May 7, 2026

laws_and_bills.name: SB26-102 Large-Load Data Centers
laws_and_bills.what: Would have required data centers over 30 MW (or 60 MW combined) to match 100% of use with renewable power from 2031, pay upfront or sign 15-year contracts, report energy and water use, and banned economic development rates; postponed indefinitely 9-0 by Senate Transportation & Energy Committee on May 11, 2026

laws_and_bills.name: 2025 data center sales tax incentive bill (number not confirmed)
laws_and_bills.what: Passed its first committee but was defeated in the appropriations committee

local_rules.what: 30-day moratorium adopted late January 2026 after inquiries from two developers; six-month moratorium to be considered
Data center planning and permitting rules adopted in 2026 (prompted by the Windsor proposal): no development in agricultural zones, water conservation plans and adequate power required
City Council rejected an outright ban on new data center construction; instead adopted a rule banning evaporative cooling (does not affect QTS's already-permitted operations)
Voted in June 2026 to cap data center energy use at 5% of the region's grid, or 100 MW
One-year moratorium on new data center permits; does not affect permitted or under-construction projects
Temporary moratorium citing wildland-urban interface, water supply, environment and community health
Temporary pause on data centers (details not given)
Proposed six-month suspension for facilities needing 10 MW or more with industrial-scale cooling
local_rules.status: proposed; council expected to act Sept. 15, 2026 (outcome not checked)

local_rules.what: Most council members favored a 6-12 month data center moratorium at a July 22, 2026 planning meeting
Commissioners directed the county attorney to draft a six-month moratorium on wind, solar, battery and data center permits until new rules and fees are adopted
Planning Commission conditions on Project Taurus: 50 MW cap, closed-loop water, noise monitoring; council decision on appeals delayed to April 13, 2027
